body:
You're right. The current alt-svc code is just a switch without fall-back logic. Not good enough.

>  Only add the alt-svc to the cache when curl determines that the service is reachable. This is what Chrome and Firefox do.

Well, that would basically just force us to have two caches since we still need to store the information about all the *possible* alternatives until they've been verified. I don't think that's good approach. Also, an alternative that works now can suddenly not work the next time, or vice versa.

>   Always add the alt-svc to cache (which is what curl does today), but then fall back to the original origin if the alt-svc isn't reachable. This is like how the IPv6 to IPv4 fallback works.

In my mind this is the most sensible way to go about it. I presume that actually will rather be translated into a *list* of options to try in a given order until one works, as there can be several listed alternatives and the "un-alternative" version would then be the last to try...

Here's a relevant issue report in Firefox regarding their plans for alt-svc use:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1498663
That still sounds like "ideas" rather than "plans", but sure. I don't think we should race all alternatives as our first option.

for completeness - same behaviour observed with nghttp2

`curl 7.69.1-DEV (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/7.69.1-DEV OpenSSL/1.1.1d c-ares/1.14.0 libssh2/1.8.0 nghttp2/1.30.0 ngtcp2/0.1.90 nghttp3/0.1.90`

investigating

leaning towards implementing the following fall back

1. check all alt-svc 
2. on failure of all #1 use original origin

Network connections are transient we make no assumptions about state and continue to push alt-svc to cache  alt-svc to the cache. 

Will also investigate implementing 'persist' behaviour which may have some part to play here ... note - 'persist' has no default value defined in the spec.

Sounds fair. If there are more than one alternative to try, it also becomes interesting in which order why try them...

On default "persist", section 3.1 says:

>   By default, cached alternative services will be cleared when the
>   client detects a network change.  Alternative services that are
>  intended to be longer lived (such as those that are not specific to
>   the client access network) can carry the "persist" parameter with a
>   value "1" as a hint that the service is potentially useful beyond a
>   network configuration change.

... which sure sounds like persist is 0 by default.
